thread:
alex_support: Heads up — Acme sent an embeddings request that's returning 1536 dims while their app expects 1024. They're seeing a downstream shape error. I attached the request/response they logged.

jordan_oncall_ml: Got the logs? can you paste the raw headers and model id from our side?

alex_support: Pasted below. Looks like their client sets `X-Org-Key: org_acme` and also `X-Project-Id: proj-legacy-abc`. Our routing chose `text-embedding-1536-large` (legacy catalog) instead of `redwood-embed-v1-1024` which their project is allowed to use.

```
REQUEST: POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX
X-Org-Key: org_acme
X-Project-Id: proj-legacy-abc
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "auto", "input": "..." }

RESPONSE: 200 OK
{ "model": "text-embedding-1536-large", "embedding": [ ... length 1536 ... ] }
```

maya_platform: Ah — looks like `auto` model resolution path used org-level default model binding and ignored project-level override when both headers present. We had a fallback rule: org header wins unless explicit `model` param set.

jordan_oncall_ml: That explains the dim mismatch. Customer's app hardcodes 1024 vector size. They upgraded project keys recently but still sending the old `X-Project-Id`. Our resolution picks org default which is the 1536 model.

alex_support: Customer says they only updated API key in their env but a sidecar was still injecting `X-Project-Id=proj-legacy-abc` from old config. Repro steps below.

bob_acme_cust: Confirm — we migrated last week and updated `AUTH_KEY`, but our build pipeline step `inject-metadata` was still adding the old project header. We'll remove that short-term.

alex_support: Short-term mitigation: ask customer to remove the stale `X-Project-Id` header or explicitly set `model: \"redwood-embed-v1-1024\"` in request. Long-term: we should change resolution priority to prefer explicit project header over org default for `auto` mode, or at least log ambiguous header combos.

maya_platform: Agree. I'll open a PR to: 1) tighten resolution precedence (project header > org header when both present), 2) add a deprecation log when `auto` picks org default while project key exists, 3) add a short-circuit that returns a hint in response when dims differ from project expected dims.

infra_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1194 — "auto model resolution: header precedence causes dimension mismatch" assigned to maya_platform.

sam_billing: FYI billing note — requests routed to `text-embedding-1536-large` are billed under org_acme default billing account. If we change resolution precedence, usage might shift to customer's project billing. We should coordinate credits.

alex_support: Customer impacted: 2 failed deploys yesterday, ~120k tokens worth of compute on the wrong model. Requested a goodwill credit. @sam_billing can you estimate credit and handle with Acme?

sam_billing: I'll pull charges and propose a credit. Tentative: waive the delta for those two deploys. Will confirm by EOD.

jordan_oncall_ml: For repro in staging: simulate headers in curl, verify model selection logic. Example: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_test_xxx" \n  -H "X-Org-Key: org_acme" \n  -H "X-Project-Id: proj-legacy-abc" \n  -d '{"input":"hello","model":"auto"}'
```

maya_platform: I'll include unit tests around header combos and add a telemetry metric for "ambiguous-header-auto-resolution" so we can find other customers affected.

alex_support: Sounds good. I'll update Acme with the workaround and expected timeline for the fix. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
